excerpts.author: jsign
excerpts.content:
mmm i think the `count` might be a problem to fix the `excess` to get the fixed fee we want (IIUC you're referring to that bullet in my list?).
In `builder_exits` the fee also adds `count - target` within the block, and doesn't only wait until `excess` is updated. before the fork the `count` never resets, so that wouldn't guarantee the fixed fee.

And `count` is only reset to 0 in the system call in existing system contracts, so whenever the fork activates the first system call would add the count of all the registrations before the fork to `excess`.

excerpts.author: jsign
excerpts.content:
<@543900561460822016> do you have any opinion about this? (i.e. moving the leanxmss-evm-verifier to sys-asm, i.e.^2 geas). 

The current verifier is in Solidity but mainly unrolled loops and mostly all assembly anyway (see [here](https://github.com/ethereum/leanxmss-evm-verifier/blob/main/contracts/src/LeanXmss.sol)).

I think there are some good argument of not putting all this into sys-asm (lmk), might be simpler to make the bytecode part of the system contract which:
1. Avoid the STATICCALL
2. Just avoid having another "indirect" system contract we have to deploy etc.

I personally don't have a strong opinion. But if feels good to put it all in sys-asm, I'm also happy to do the change (apart from the queuing changes being discussed).
